title: Three audit figures: does the mass add up, what was actually run, and where does the equilibrium baseline fail?
summary: A Sankey ledger, a design-of-experiments map and a four-panel parity plot are the rigour figures of an experimental campaign. They do not show a result; they show whether the results can be trusted, what they cover, and which simple model is not enough.

media.alt: Two Sankey diagrams of representative runs, in kg per hour. Left, lignite plus steam, closure 0.985: fuel 6.6, air 14.9 and steam 1.3 enter; dry gas 15.1, char 0.6, water 1.4 and ash 1.8 leave. Right, lignite with 7 percent MgCO3 and steam, closure 0.921: fuel 6.7, air 12.8, steam 1.3 in; dry gas 15.3, char 0.6, water 1.4, ash 1.8 out.

source.caption: Mass-balance Sankey diagram
source.note: Group explainer for the three rigor figures: the representative mass-balance Sankey, the operating map of the 14 runs in (SBR, equivalence ratio) coloured by H2 yield, and the equilibrium parity plot for H2, CO, CO2 and CH4. See 'As drawn' for a closure value that the printed numbers do not reproduce.

read_the_figure.question: Is the experimental data credible (mass closes), what range of conditions does it cover, and how far off is a simple equilibrium prediction from the measurement?
read_the_figure.axes: Sankey (03): flow widths proportional to mass flow in kg/h; inputs (fuel, air, steam) on the left and bottom, outputs (dry gas, char, water, ash) on the right and bottom; the title gives the run and its closure ratio. Operating map (04): x is SBR from 0 to about 0.47, y is the equivalence ratio ER from about 0.39 to 0.52; circles are lignite plus steam, squares are lignite plus 7% MgCO3 plus steam; colour is H2 in vol% from about 23 to 35. Parity (06): four panels (H2, CO, CO2, CH4), x measured and y predicted in vol% dry, a dashed y = x line, open symbols for raw equilibrium and filled symbols for quasi-equilibrium, blue for lignite plus steam and orange for the catalyst case.
look_at: Sankey: add the arrows. Mass in should equal mass out; the closure ratio in the title is out over in. The two panels show two runs at the same SBR level 3, differing in catalyst.

Operating map: the 14 points are not on a regular grid. The catalyst runs (squares) sit lower in ER than the no-catalyst runs (circles): 0.39 to 0.47 against 0.44 to 0.51. The two brightest points, the H2 maxima, are at SBR about 0.25.

Parity: distance from the dashed line is the model error. Raw-equilibrium points for H2 and CO sit near zero predicted against 7 to 35 measured; quasi-equilibrium points are much closer but still systematically on one side of the line.
Species directions: H2 under-predicted, CO over-predicted by quasi-equilibrium, CO2 over-predicted by raw equilibrium and CH4 over-predicted by raw but close for quasi.
read_the_figure.proves: That mass is accounted for to within the stated closure; that the campaign covers a range of SBR and ER, not a grid; and that a pure equilibrium assumption is not a sufficient model of this gasifier, since its predictions fall off the diagonal in all four species.
if_wrong: Closure well below 1: some stream is not measured, or the sampling is biased. Conclusions based on gas composition inherit that uncertainty.
A map in which two factors move together (here ER and catalyst, and SBR with ER) cannot attribute an effect to one factor.
Predicted values on the diagonal for the wrong reason: a good parity plot can hide compensating errors, so look at every species.
must_check: The definition of closure (which streams, mass or elements, wet or dry).
The arrows in the Sankey add up to the printed closure.
Whether ER was controlled or only recorded, since it changes along with SBR in the map.
That the parity axes in each panel have equal ranges so the diagonal is at 45 degrees; they do here, but the four panels have different ranges from each other.
That a model-error statistic (bias, RMSE) is printed; it is not here.
as_drawn: Sankey, left (lignite plus steam): in 6.6 + 14.9 + 1.3 = 22.8 kg/h, out 15.1 + 0.6 + 1.4 + 1.8 = 18.9 kg/h. The ratio of the printed numbers is 18.9 / 22.8 = 0.83, not the printed 0.985. Right (catalyst): in 6.7 + 12.8 + 1.3 = 20.8, out 15.3 + 0.6 + 1.4 + 1.8 = 19.1, ratio 0.918, close to the printed 0.921. The left panel's closure does not follow from its printed flows; it may use a different basis or a mislabelled flow.

Air-to-fuel check against the map: left A/F = 14.9 / 6.6 = 2.26 and the map's ER at SBR 0.2 for no catalyst is about 0.50, implying a stoichiometric A/F of 2.26 / 0.50 = 4.5; right 12.8 / 6.7 = 1.91 at ER about 0.42 gives 4.5 again. The two runs are consistent with each other and with the map. SBR from the Sankey is 1.3 / 6.6 = 0.20 and 1.3 / 6.7 = 0.19, in line with the map.

Parity, read off by eye (vol% dry): measured H2 23 to 35, raw prediction 0 to 6, quasi prediction 12 to 21; measured CO 7.5 to 12, quasi 11 to 13.5; measured CO2 8 to 23, raw 23 to 28, quasi 17 to 22; measured CH4 1.1 to 2.7, raw 1 to 7.5, quasi 1 to 2.5. Measured H2, CO, CO2 and CH4 together are about 47 to 50 vol%, the remainder being N2 from the air.

terms.meaning: Mass out divided by mass in. One means everything is accounted for.
A flow diagram in which the width of each band is proportional to the quantity that flows.
Actual air-to-fuel ratio divided by the stoichiometric air-to-fuel ratio. Below one is fuel-rich; gasifiers run at about 0.2 to 0.5.
A plan for choosing run conditions so that effects of several factors can be separated.
A prediction of the gas composition at the minimum of the Gibbs energy for the given elements and temperature, ignoring rates.
An equilibrium calculation modified to allow for the fact that the real gas does not reach equilibrium. The figure's legend separates it from raw equilibrium.
Predicted against measured with a y = x line; points on the line are perfect.
Composition after the water has been removed from the sample, so that species add to 100 percent.

remember: Closure is out over in; add the printed numbers to check it.
Equivalence ratio is relative to stoichiometric air: A/F actual over A/F stoichiometric.
In a non-grid design, factors move together; say which ones.
A parity plot hides compensating errors; read each species.
Equilibrium predicts where chemistry ends if it had unlimited time; a real gasifier does not have it.

understand.title: Why a ledger is evidence
understand.text: A Sankey is a picture of an equation: inputs equal outputs. If the arrows do not add up, the picture is telling you something about the measurement, not the gasifier. This is the first figure to check before trusting any gas composition.

understand.title: Why map the runs
understand.text: Fourteen runs cannot cover a three-dimensional space densely, so a map shows what was covered. It also shows confounding: the catalyst runs sit at a lower ER, so a difference between them may come from ER, not the catalyst.

understand.title: Why equilibrium fails
understand.text: Equilibrium needs enough time and temperature for every reaction. At these temperatures the gas leaves with CH4 and CO2 left over and H2 below equilibrium for some species and above for others. The deviation tells you which reactions are rate limited.

steps.title: Closure
steps.tex: \epsilon=\frac{\dot m_{\mathrm{gas}}+\dot m_{\mathrm{char}}+\dot m_{\mathrm{water}}+\dot m_{\mathrm{ash}}}{\dot m_{\mathrm{fuel}}+\dot m_{\mathrm{air}}+\dot m_{\mathrm{steam}}}
steps.note: Mass balance for a steady process. For the right-hand run, 19.1 / 20.8 = 0.918.

steps.title: Equivalence ratio from flows
steps.note: Given the flows and the ER on the map, the stoichiometric air-to-fuel ratio that the data imply is about 4.5 kg per kg. This check uses printed and read-off numbers only.

steps.title: Equilibrium composition
steps.note: Gibbs-energy minimisation subject to element balances (a_ji atoms of element j in species i, b_j the supplied amount). It is the standard way to get an equilibrium composition at a given temperature and pressure.

steps.title: Parity errors
steps.note: Two numbers to print beside every parity plot. Bias says which side of the diagonal the model sits on, RMSE how far off it is on average.

steps.title: Species must add to one
steps.note: On a dry basis the species fractions add to one. The four panels cover about half of the measured gas; the rest is N2, which the gas chromatograph also measures.

worked.title: Check closure and ER on the catalyst run
worked.problem: Right-hand Sankey: fuel 6.7, air 12.8, steam 1.3 in; gas 15.3, char 0.6, water 1.4, ash 1.8 out (kg/h). Find the closure and the SBR, and compare with the printed 0.921.
worked.answer: Closure 0.918, within rounding of the printed 0.921. Doing the same for the left-hand run gives 0.83, not 0.985, which should be checked.

analyze.q: The left Sankey's printed flows give a closure of 0.83, the printed value is 0.985. List three explanations and the check that would separate them.
analyze.hint: A mislabelled flow, a different basis for closure (elements, dry gas), an unlabelled stream such as tar.

analyze.q: On the map the catalyst runs sit at lower ER. How could this change the interpretation of the catalyst's effect on H2?
analyze.hint: ER also controls the combustion-zone temperature.

analyze.q: In the parity plot, raw equilibrium predicts H2 near zero while quasi-equilibrium predicts 12 to 21. What does that suggest about whether the gas is near equilibrium at the exit?
analyze.hint: Which of the two models is closer to the diagonal, and for which species?

evaluate.q: Is a parity plot with no bias or RMSE sufficient to reject a model?
evaluate.hint: Distance from the diagonal is visible, but the size of the error is not stated.

evaluate.q: With 14 runs in two series and three varying factors, how much would you trust a regression of H2 on SBR alone?
evaluate.hint: Think of confounding and seven points per series.

create: Redraw the Sankey so that the closure is computed from the arrows and printed with the unmeasured remainder shown as its own band.
Add a column to the operating map for the measured combustion-zone temperature, and propose the next two runs that would decouple ER from SBR.

checks.answer: The fraction of the input mass that is accounted for in the measured outputs; a value of one means a perfectly closed balance.

checks.q: Streams in: 6.7, 12.8 and 1.3 kg/h; out: 15.3, 0.6, 1.4 and 1.8. What is the closure?
Why is a design that changes ER and catalyst together hard to interpret?
checks.answer: An effect on H2 could come from either; without runs that vary them separately the effects are confounded.

checks.q: Quasi-equilibrium points are closer to the diagonal than raw equilibrium points. Is the quasi model therefore correct?
checks.answer: No. It is better but still off for H2 and CO, and a model can be closer for the wrong reasons; bias and RMSE per species are needed.

checks.q: How would you present model error for the four species in one figure?
checks.answer: Print bias and RMSE in each parity panel, or plot residuals against the measured value so that structure is visible.

provenance.notes: Standard theory only. The legend names 'raw equilibrium' and 'quasi-equilibrium'; only the generic idea is taught, nothing of how the quasi-equilibrium variant is built. For the owner: the closure printed for the left Sankey (0.985) does not follow from its printed flows (0.83); the right one does (0.918 against 0.921). The page text quotes a closure range of 0.920 to 0.995 over 14 runs.
